name: Milvus
summary: A cloud-native vector database that models collections of vector and scalar data, builds selectable ANN indexes, separates query and data processing services, and exposes client and administration interfaces.

features.name: Typed collection and field schema
features.description: Milvus collections define vector fields together with scalar data such as integers, strings, and JSON objects; client APIs create collections, insert records, and search with selected output fields.
benefits: Keeps vector and metadata attributes under one collection contract
Supports filtering and retrieval of associated scalar fields
costs: Schema and dimension choices constrain later data and index operations
Vector and scalar semantics must remain aligned across clients and services

features.name: Selectable ANN index lifecycle
features.description: Milvus supports multiple vector index families, including HNSW, IVF, FLAT, SCANN, and DiskANN, with documented quantization and mmap-related options; index selection is part of serving a collection.
benefits: Provides workload-specific choices between exact and approximate search structures
Separates vector search structure selection from collection data modeling
costs: Index choice creates build, memory, recall, and update trade-offs
Different index families expose different operational requirements

features.name: Separated query and data services
features.description: Milvus documents an architecture that separates compute for query and data processing from storage, allowing query nodes and data nodes to scale independently in a distributed deployment.
benefits: Allows read-heavy and write-heavy capacity to be scaled separately
Creates explicit service and recovery boundaries around vector data processing
costs: Cross-service coordination and consistency become deployment concerns
Distributed operation requires orchestration, storage, and network resources

features.name: Client and administration interfaces
features.description: Milvus exposes SDK/client operations for collection creation, insertion, and search, while its documented ecosystem includes administration and monitoring tools such as Attu, Birdwatcher, and Prometheus/Grafana integrations.
benefits: Separates application data-plane operations from operational control paths
Provides language and deployment integration points
costs: Client, server, and administration versions must remain compatible
Operational tooling observes and controls a distributed system with multiple failure boundaries

mathematical_views.question: How do vector and scalar fields form a typed collection that supports insertion, filtering, and nearest-neighbor search?
assumptions: Records satisfy the declared field and vector dimensions
Search predicates and output fields are interpreted according to the collection schema
The view abstracts serialization and storage encoding

mathematical_views.question: How does an index family refine a collection into a search structure while exposing a recall/resource trade-off?
assumptions: The index implements the documented distance and query semantics
Exact FLAT and approximate families are compared structurally, not by unmeasured performance
Build and load states are explicit lifecycle states

mathematical_views.question: Which data, query, storage, and coordinator states must compose for an inserted vector to become searchable?
assumptions: Service roles and storage boundaries are modeled explicitly
Consistency and freshness depend on configured deployment behavior
The model does not claim a universal visibility latency

costs: Index-specific build, memory, and recall trade-offs
